Alpha 1.0.1 (a world worth seeing)

  • Heroes and equipment feel crafted: tailored armor and robes, open headwear, cleaner weapon edges, fitted shoulders and cuffs, smaller mounted gems, and restrained magical accents refine all four classes. Necks remain connected when necklaces replace costume collars. Cloth, leather, wood, and metal separate more clearly under shared procedural reflection lighting.
  • Your build takes center stage: the character sheet now includes a rotatable, fully equipped 3D preview between fourteen keyboard-accessible slots. It renders on demand and keeps controls reachable on small screens.
  • A calmer, clearer interface: login and class choice, menus, HUD, journals, skills, services, and social panels share an ink-and-brass palette, more consistent spacing, readable layers, and responsive scrolling. Item icons retain their original colors instead of being multiplied by rarity tint.
  • Adventure choices are easier to read: separate Dungeons and Raids tabs show party authority, elemental raid cards, Chronicle unlock requirements, and crystal-repair guidance. Auction controls match the theme, with readable cards on narrow screens.
  • The world supports the action: Lanternhold paving and Gloamwood soil have finer, less distracting patterns that align between High and Low settings. Boss-warning edges remain visible at their exact danger radius throughout the pulse.
  • The Dark King has his own silhouette: Malachar wears black iron, a fractured crown and royal mantle, carries an oathbreaker sword, and bears the four bound elements. His production model retains its full combat animation rig.
  • Clean controls and resource lifetime: Enter and Space activate focused menu controls without stealing chat focus or casting; Escape closes the portal menu without opening pause, and chat remains permanent. Corrected camera-impact timing and boss-label texture cleanup, batched rigid equipment pieces, and whole-frame render counters support smoother, measurable play.
  • Verified locally: class/equipment and High/Low visual checks, responsive keyboard menus, real-server movement and multiplayer combat, and repeated ten-hero rendering workloads accompany this pass. The busy-scene profile is a rendering fixture, not a claim that a full ten-player raid has been completed. Asset generation advances to 2026-09-04-11.

Alpha 1.0.0 (the worlds answer together)

  • Multiplayer has a social backbone: structured world, party, guild, whisper, and system chat now includes reconnect history, reply convenience, ignore/block controls, Mongo-backed reports, party readiness, role and health display, and configurable loot rules.
  • Trustworthy player trade: both-confirm direct trade uses server-owned escrow, while auction settlement independently tracks item and seller claims to prevent duplicate delivery or lost payout during retries and races.
  • Guilds are persistent institutions: create, invite, roster, rank, MOTD, leadership, bank, audit, guild chat, and seasonal dungeon leaderboard flows survive reconnects; compact guild identity now appears in chat, social surfaces, and remote nameplates.
  • PvP is genuinely playable: the central relationship resolver powers safe zones, duels, surrender and first-down outcomes, opt-in overworld flagging, 1v1 and 2v2 arenas, seasonal profiles, cosmetic-first rewards, balance scalars, and disconnect penalties.
  • The cap has a long tail: level-100 characters earn Resonance ranks, the Umbral Nexus becomes the fifth dungeon, and the 5–10-player Dark Realm raid has an ISO-week lockout and its own reward path.
  • The Fourfold Chronicle tells Eidolon's central story: every character begins a 15-chapter campaign without a quest-giver handoff, recovers soulbound relics across Earth, Water, Fire, and Air, clears each realm dungeon to expose a separate crystal raid, then completes all four raids and protects Artificer Maelin through three-wave repair Vigils.
  • Resonance opens the endgame: only four restored crystals can reveal the Umbral Nexus and stabilize the Dark Realm portal. Malachar explains his attempt to enslave Eidolon's elements during a four-phase finale where Orun, Neris, Pyralis, and Aeral each materially aid the raid.
  • The architecture can carry the game: the four former orchestration hotspots are below their roadmap limits, per-instance dungeon locking is documented and tested, handlers are registered with admission/rate policies, and the state protocol advances to EDPB version 2 for level-cap XP.
  • Persistence and operations are explicit: seven ordered Mongo migrations, required indexes, repository-owned character mapping, report administration, runtime health telemetry, real multi-client load scenarios, benchmarks, and a scheduled 100-client 24-hour soak replace implicit release assumptions.
  • Exploit surfaces were swept: progression bounds, dungeon re-entry, weekly rewards, proximity credit, auction concurrency, direct-trade confirmation, guild-bank races, malformed frames, oversized traffic, and client action contracts now have server-side guards and regression coverage.
  • Chat stays with the player: Escape releases chat focus and closes other windows without hiding the permanent transcript.
  • The Quest Giver steps into view: the Lanternhold guide now stands fully outside the Ashen Smithy doorway and remains aligned across server state, offline play, minimap, and world map.
  • Clients receive Alpha 1.0: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-04-10.

Alpha 0.90.0 milestone (the foundation holds)

  • Characters survive interrupted journeys: reconnect, session resume, dungeon-room restoration, and interrupted crystal Vigil recovery preserve authoritative progress instead of silently restarting completed work.
  • Persistence has an upgrade path: ordered Mongo migrations, required indexes, and repository-owned character mapping protect existing players as the world schema evolves.
  • The protocol has enforceable boundaries: EDPB version 2, registered handlers, authentication rules, payload limits, per-message rate policies, and outbound backpressure keep malformed or excessive traffic from becoming gameplay authority.
  • Known duplication routes are closed: auctions, direct trade, guild banking, progression, raid rewards, loot ownership, and dungeon re-entry are guarded by server-side validation and regression coverage.
  • Release confidence is repeatable: multi-client load scenarios, hot-path benchmarks, race tests, real-browser gates, accessibility checks, and a scheduled 100-client soak define the final pre-beta standard.

Alpha 0.80.0 milestone (the endgame answers)

  • Level 100 begins a new progression path: Resonance ranks and Power, Ward, and Fortune traits turn experience beyond the cap into persistent specialization.
  • The Umbral Nexus opens as a fifth dungeon: new dissonant enemies, Memory Fracture danger fields, and the Eidolon Devourer connect the elemental journey to the Dark Realm.
  • Every crystal has a true raid: Rootheart Sanctum, Tidestar Confluence, Ember Crown Crucible, and Skyglass Eyrie are separate 5–10-player assaults unlocked by their matching realm dungeons.
  • Raid victory requires restoration: defeating each crystal guardian begins Artificer Maelin's three-wave Vigil, and the crystal is not credited until every counterattack is cleared.
  • The Dark King becomes the weekly summit: the Dark Realm raid adds a personal weekly reward path and a four-phase Malachar encounter aided by Orun, Neris, Pyralis, and Aeral.

Alpha 0.70.0 milestone (the banners cross)

  • Combat allegiance is authoritative: one server relationship resolver decides friendly, hostile, duel, arena, party, guild, and safe-zone interactions.
  • Duels have complete stakes and closure: challenge, accept, decline, surrender, cancel, and first-down outcomes support competitive fights without applying PvE death loss.
  • Arenas support real team formats: dedicated 1v1 and 2v2 instances isolate matches from the overworld and apply PvP-specific balance scalars.
  • Competition persists across sessions: seasonal rating, wins, losses, streaks, honor, cosmetic-first rewards, leaderboards, and queue or disconnect penalties form the ranked loop.
  • The world can become dangerous by choice: opt-in overworld PvP respects protected town space and clearly distinguishes hostile and friendly players through targets and nameplates.

Alpha 0.60.0 milestone (the guild lanterns are lit)

  • Guilds become persistent institutions: players can create, invite, join, leave, remove members, set ranks and MOTDs, transfer leadership, recover inactive leadership, and disband.
  • Ranks carry real responsibility: Leader, Officer, and Member permissions control governance and shared-resource actions.
  • Guildmates remain connected across Eidolon: guild chat and presence work across regions, dungeons, raids, reconnects, and separate instances.
  • The guild bank is accountable: shared items and gold use serialized mutations, permission checks, withdrawal limits, and a durable audit history.
  • Guild identity is visible: tags appear in chat, social panels, remote nameplates, and guild-associated dungeon leaderboards.

Alpha 0.50.0 milestone (no hero walks alone)

  • Chat becomes a multiplayer system: world, party, guild, whisper, and system channels include reconnect history, reply support, ignore, block, moderation reports, and rate protection.
  • Parties can organize difficult content: roles, ready checks, nearby health presentation, persistent membership, and configurable free-for-all or master-loot rules support coordinated play.
  • Direct exchange is trustworthy: both players must confirm the same server-owned offer, and any item or gold change invalidates prior confirmation before atomic settlement.
  • The Trading House is easier to use: category filters and clearer listing flows help players find the gear and materials they actually need.
  • The economy can be balanced from evidence: authoritative gold-source and gold-sink telemetry exposes where wealth enters, moves through, and leaves the world.

Patch 0.41.0.36 (the dawnwarden casts off the cowl)

  • The friar silhouette is gone: the Cleric's pale circular collar, rear coif, long ivory stole, broad burial cloak, and ankle-length bell vestments have been removed.
  • A dawnwarden takes her place: swept auburn hair, a visible bun and temple locks, long side braids, warm facial planes, brows, paired holy eyes, and defined lips keep the adult heroine readable at gameplay distance.
  • Sun-templar armor shapes the class: fitted dual reliquary breastplates, a narrow armored waist, hip faulds, split wine-red war skirt and cape, long plated legs, gold diadem, and seven-ray sun crown replace the monastic costume language.
  • Equipment follows the heroine: Cleric helmets, chest pieces, and pauldrons now use a tighter class-specific fit; her full face, temple hair, and exterior braids remain visible around headgear even with all fourteen slots equipped.
  • The whole sacred rig remains intact: all 18 equipment attachment regions, every generated item family, mace and censer restoration, Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, Death, local and remote actors, hitboxes, pooling, and shared geometry continue through the same contracts.
  • The cowl cannot quietly return: structural coverage forbids the old coif, stole, and burial cloak, requires every new dawnwarden component, and validates the complete equipped and unequipped silhouettes in hardware Chrome.
  • Only presentation changed: Cleric statistics, abilities, movement, combat authority, synchronization, progression, equipment data, and saved characters are unchanged.
  • Clients receive the new dawnwarden: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-36.

Patch 0.41.0.35 (the grave learns the weight of steel)

  • The first bones remain the measure: level 1–10 Skeleton health, damage, and swing timing are unchanged and now anchor the complete enemy progression curve.
  • Higher realms answer post-squish heroes: every Imp, Demon Orc, Construct, Inferno Titan, Moonfrost creature, Cinder Wastes foe, and Stormcrown enemy now grows from one level-based health and damage budget instead of disconnected pre-squish stat blocks.
  • Gear quality changes the shape of a fight: same-level mixed uncommon/rare equipment lands in a steady middle encounter band, low or missing gear creates meaningful pressure, and full legendary, upgraded, potency-enhanced equipment makes ordinary same-level enemies decisively easy.
  • Creature identity survives the squish: glass cannons, bruisers, tanks, and swift attackers retain bounded family-specific health, damage, and movement differences without breaking the shared progression curve.
  • Dungeons no longer demand obsolete numbers: normal packs, elite rooms, sequential bosses, run levels, and Normal/Heroic/Mythic difficulty now compose from the same post-squish foundation; the old million-Vitality and accidental extra ×10 boss assumptions are gone.
  • Elite danger and elite rewards agree: Fire, Air, Verdant, and Abyssal elite-room spawns now carry explicit elite identity alongside their intended combat multiplier, allowing the existing elite loot path to recognize all of them.
  • Slows cannot heal the enemy: applying or expiring temporary movement effects no longer adds player-only level health, replaces authored hostile speed, or enables enemy regeneration during combat.
  • The curve is guarded end to end: server regression coverage checks every overworld family against low, medium, and optimized gear envelopes, preserves the exact Skeleton anchor, and verifies elite, dungeon, boss, run-level, difficulty, and debuff transitions.
  • Clients receive the new balance ledger: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-35.

Patch 0.41.0.34 (two heroines step from the veil)

  • The shadeblade shows her face: the Rogue is now an adult female hero with a sharper faceted face, paired emerald eyes, brows, lips, swept dark hair, a side braid, deeper hood framing, and a more agile shoulder–waist–hip silhouette.
  • The last sun crowns a priestess: the Cleric is now an adult female hero with warm facial features, paired holy eyes, a braided crown and side plaits, a rear coif, and a strong feminine silhouette beneath practical reliquary armor.
  • Armor still fits the bearer: all 18 attachment regions and every equipment family retain exact local and remote placement; default hair and ornaments hide beneath equipped headgear while faces and paired eyes remain readable.
  • Beauty does not change battle: hitboxes, authoritative movement, abilities, animation timing, equipment replication, class balance, and saved characters are unchanged. Dedicated High and Low hardware renders validate both redesigned heroes in every animation state.
  • Clients receive the new silhouettes: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-34.
